prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: acceptance/transfer through aircraft-loading handoff; excludes loading beyond Outbound Load Control Desk. Objectives: safety/accuracy/throughput/cutoffs; no explicit modes. Item recipients unspecified. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance/initiates processing/sends Oversize Exception Ticket. Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable passenger/flight-linked tags/Calibration Witness Tag. Transfer Bag Feeder records arrivals/sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds pending screening/onward-handling confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight/routing records/Flight Cutoff Advisory; maintains identifiers/destinations/departure times/revisions, airline dispatch targets/connection windows/time-stamped changes. Dispatch time prioritizes bags; departure time is passenger-facing. Baggage Control System (Velvet) validates acceptance/transfer/flight assignments against current schedules; coordinates visibility/routing, approved screening profiles/time-effective sort plans. Alternatives require approval, valid screening/timing; prefer sufficient capacity/time; prohibit blocked/unavailable releases. Unresolved destinations/handling-limit violations divert to Secondary Inspection Chute, segregated from outbound flows; access requires authorized duties. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates availability/plan, permits restricted-equipment induction, produces Recovery Route Card. Induction Tray Conveyor preserves spacing/identification; jam/open-door/downstream-unready interlocks stop feeds. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner verify identities/acquire images/return dispositions; South provides independent reads/Manual Rescan Receipt. Maintain record quality/alarms; incomplete examinations never clear; mismatches block identity-dependent routes. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity/routes by destination/screening; sends Chute Occupancy Note near capacity. Image Resolution Desk staff resolve image holds/record dispositions. Pending/alarmed/missing-record bags require examination/control, never make-up; return requires agreed identity/outcome/authorization. Bag Reconciliation Station compares active records/flags discrepancies/sends Bag Match Query. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor selection follows plan/capacity. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages authorized/cleared bags within flight window/reports constrained capacity. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms readiness; Airline Ramp Coordinator accepts handoff/sends authorized Carousel Release Slip. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) coordinates recovery/staffing/readiness; receives isolation notices, sets congestion thresholds/overload response, authorizes recovery after correction. Congestion uses availability/stops/incoming rate.

Document units:
S109: Baggage Control System applies cutoff profiles configured for each carrier, flight, and operating condition.
S110: A bag accepted before cutoff retains its assigned flight unless a subsequent schedule or operational change requires reassessment.
S111: When schedule revisions move a departure earlier, Baggage Operations Supervisor reviews affected flights and directs priority adjustments.
S112: Cutoff values account for screening, sortation, make-up, and transfer handling allowances rather than only aircraft departure.
S113: Baggage Control System receives the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
S114: Baggage Control System compares remaining processing time with route-specific handling estimates.
S115: Bags with confirmed screening clearance may proceed to flight-specific sort destinations when capacity is available.
S116: Bags awaiting screening are held from final flight induction even when their scheduled departure is near.
S117: North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner record screening outcomes for inducted bags.
S118: The Image Resolution Desk reviews unresolved images, and final routing remains withheld until disposition is recorded.
S119: A positive threat indication suspends ordinary routing until the authorized security disposition is entered.
S120: Explosives Response Team produces the Custody Seal Log.
S121: When screening disposition is pending, Baggage Control System preserves a recoverable bag-to-flight association rather than releasing the bag to make-up.
S122: Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes eligible bags according to flight assignment and current cutoff priority.
S123: Concourse Zone Controller coordinates induction demand with available conveyor capacity across the operating area.
S124: Induction Tray Conveyor admits bags in priority order, subject to scan confirmation and safe spacing.
S125: East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor receive flight groups according to active allocation rules.
S126: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit presents bags for outbound loading only after flight grouping and screening status are confirmed.
S127: Outbound Load Control Desk uses planned dispatch time and load-close targets to monitor whether assigned bags can be accepted.
S128: Airline Ramp Coordinator reports changes to loading readiness that could alter the usable cutoff.
S129: Baggage Operations Supervisor may defer lower-priority bags when a flight's remaining processing window is insufficient.
S130: Bags missing the active flight cutoff are held for reassignment or recovery rather than routed into an unavailable departure build.
S131: Make-up allocation begins when the active flight assignment and available build positions are confirmed.
